content.value_statement: Starting an interactive survival story can require careful pacing, character voice, and meaningful choices. This skill provides a structured first chapter for a stranded astronaut scenario.
actual_capabilities: Sets a crash-survival scene on an unknown planet.
Defines Stella Chen as a trained but frightened astronaut.
Guides a five-stage conversation with escalating decisions.
Provides three immediate choices with different story outcomes.
Maintains bilingual Chinese and English character dialogue.
Suggests follow-up chapters based on the player choice.
limitations: It supplies a single story chapter, not a complete game system.
It does not generate images, sound, or playable software.
It assumes the user wants the established Stella Chen setting.
It does not guarantee scientific accuracy for all fictional details.

use_cases.title: Start a survival roleplay
use_cases.description: Begin a tense first-contact scene where a player guides an injured astronaut after a crash.

use_cases.title: Practice branching dialogue
use_cases.description: Use the choices and outcomes as a model for writing responsive character conversations.

use_cases.title: Run a creative writing exercise
use_cases.description: Explore pacing, atmosphere, and emotional character development in a science-fiction scene.

prompt_templates.title: Begin the scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Start Emergency Distress Signal. Speak as Stella Chen and send the opening distress message.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an evacuation
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the crash scene. I tell Stella to evacuate immediately. Continue with short, responsive messages.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a different choice
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Emergency Distress Signal. I choose to save the communication system first. Show the consequences and preserve Stella’s voice.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this chapter structure to create a new survival scene. Keep the five stages, but change the planet, danger, and astronaut background.

output: A weak transmission begins from Stella Chen after the spacecraft crash.
Stella asks whether anyone can hear her and reports an unknown location.
The player is invited to check her safety or assess the emergency.
Stella agrees that personal safety comes first.
She exits with a survival pack as the damaged craft becomes more dangerous.
Outside, she describes an unfamiliar forest and asks for the next decision.
Stella inventories food, tools, medical supplies, and a damaged spacesuit.
She identifies possible water nearby and unexplained scanner readings.
The player chooses between seeking shelter and investigating the signal.

best_practices: Reply with a clear choice when Stella presents urgent options.
Keep player messages concise to preserve the dialogue pace.
Treat the setting as fiction and build on its established details.
anti_patterns: Do not resolve every mystery during the opening chapter.
Do not make Stella invulnerable or ignore the player choices.
Do not replace short dialogue turns with long exposition.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an interactive first chapter about an astronaut stranded after a spacecraft crash.

faq.question: Who is Stella Chen?
faq.answer: Stella Chen is the fictional astronaut character who communicates with the player.

faq.question: Can I choose Stella’s actions?
faq.answer: Yes. The chapter presents decisions about fire, evacuation, communication, shelter, and exploration.

faq.question: Is this a complete game?
faq.answer: No. It is a narrative chapter and a foundation for later survival-story scenes.

faq.question: Which languages does the character use?
faq.answer: The source dialogue primarily uses Chinese with selected English technical terms.

faq.question: Can I adapt the scenario?
faq.answer: Yes. You can reuse its pacing and branching structure for another fictional survival setting.
